name: Khellin
short: Topical khellin with UVA or simulated sunlight caused skin cancers in mice. In a vitiligo series (mostly oral khellin plus UVA), 7 of 28 had raised liver enzymes and stopped treatment.
text: In a series of 28 people with vitiligo given khellin with UVA light three times weekly (25 by mouth, 3 applied to the skin), 7 had a mild rise in liver transaminases early in treatment and their treatment was stopped; the abstract does not say which route those 7 received, and the authors reported no long-term internal organ or skin toxicity and no phototoxic skin reactions. A separate case report, published as a letter without an abstract, is titled as a marked increase of liver transaminases after khellin and UVA therapy. A systematic review of medicinal plants used for vitiligo listed khellin-related erythema, perilesional hyperpigmentation, gastrointestinal disturbances, mild rises in liver transaminases and orthostatic complaints, and noted that the trials were mainly efficacy-oriented with safety reported poorly or not at all. In an animal study, a 5% khellin cream applied to the skin of lightly pigmented hairless mice before UVA or simulated sunlight was carcinogenic, and with simulated sunlight it increased skin tumour development to a similar extent to a psoralen cream; the abstract does not report human cancer data. In contrast, an open trial in 74 people with vitiligo using khellin encapsulated in liposomes combined with UVA/UVB light reported no side effects (the abstract does not state the route). No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
